mechanism_narrative: A sustained decline in the federal funds rate signals an active monetary easing policy that reduces discount rates for equity valuation, producing positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days regardless of other macro conditions.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns following FEDFUNDS declines are not significantly positive (t-test p > 0.05) or Rank IC falls below 0.03 over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: When the unemployment rate exceeds 5.0% for two consecutive months, it indicates deteriorating labor market conditions that suppress consumer spending and corporate earnings growth, causing negative S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: 5-day forward returns remain positive when UNRATE exceeds 5.0% for two months in > 40% of instances or Rank IC < 0.03 over 2-year window.

mechanism_narrative: Simultaneous declines in housing starts and retail sales indicate a broad-based consumer demand contraction that triggers earnings revisions downward, producing negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: 20-day returns are positive when both HOUST and RSAFS decline in > 40% of cases or Rank IC < 0.03 over 3-year window.

mechanism_narrative: Industrial production below 95.0 signals manufacturing sector weakness that reduces corporate capital expenditure and profit margins, causing negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days during industrial contraction regimes.
failure_condition: 60-day returns are not significantly negative when INDPRO < 95.0 (t-test p > 0.05) or Rank IC < 0.03 over 3-year window.

mechanism_narrative: A rising trend in housing starts indicates strong consumer confidence and increased residential investment, boosting corporate revenues and producing positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days regardless of other conditions.
failure_condition: 20-day returns following HOUST increases are not significantly positive (t-test p > 0.05) or Rank IC < 0.03 over 3-year window.

mechanism_narrative: Year-over-year CPI inflation exceeding 3.0% signals persistent inflation that forces the Federal Reserve to tighten monetary policy, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: 20-day returns are not significantly negative when CPIAUCSL > 3.0% YoY (t-test p > 0.05) or Rank IC < 0.03 over 2-year window.

mechanism_narrative: Simultaneous employment growth and unemployment decline indicate a rapidly tightening labor market that accelerates wage inflation and prompts monetary tightening, causing negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: 60-day returns are positive when PAYEMS rises and UNRATE falls in > 40% of cases or Rank IC < 0.03 over 3-year window.

mechanism_narrative: High inflation (CPIAUCSL > 3.0% YoY) combined with low interest rates (FEDFUNDS < 1.0%) creates a policy dilemma that increases market uncertainty, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: 20-day returns are not significantly negative when CPIAUCSL > 3.0% YoY and FEDFUNDS < 1.0% (t-test p > 0.05) or Rank IC < 0.03 over 3-year window.
